body: As of April 10th 2025, the only parts of the island of Cyprus with Street View coverage are the British overseas territories of Akrotiri and Dhekelia, on the southern coast of the island.
Coverage in Cyprus uses Generation 4 smallcam, a low-mounted camera with a large circular blur and occasional rear antenna. Greece also has significant smallcam coverage.
Cyprus bollards resemble Turkish ones with a red front reflector and white rear reflector but are triangular with slanted tops, unlike Turkish flat bollards.
Directional signs in Cyprus are similar to Greek signs but the Greek text is not in all caps as it is in Greece.
Town entry signs feature a yellow rectangle with a red border, a speed limit sign, and the town name written in both Greek and English.
Utility poles are mainly tall, dark brown wooden poles, similar to those in Greece.
Common pole tops are either a crossbar with three insulators or five insulators attached to the pole's side, both also common in Greece.
Buildings are typically brightly painted stone with tiled or flat roofs, a feature shared with Greek architecture.
Cyprus has a Mediterranean landscape with bright exposed rock, olive trees, and green coastal farmland; terrain is mostly hilly but not mountainous.
